page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.94-376 is a compute-focused flexible virtual machine instance powered by AMD EPYC 9J45 processors on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration provisions 94 dedicated physical cores running at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz, exposing 188 vCPUs via two threads per core. System memory totals 376.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB of RAM allocated per vCPU.

The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage and features zero GPU accelerators. Persistent data persistence and high-throughput IOPS depend entirely on remote block volumes or external network storage solutions. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The resource profile prioritizes raw thread capacity over large memory footprints or hardware accelerators, requiring infrastructure planning for external storage latency.

With high parallel core density and a tight memory balance, this instance type delivers cost-effective compute capacity for heavily threaded, CPU-bound workloads. Appropriate use cases include batch processing pipelines, continuous integration and compilation workflows, video transcoding, parallel numerical simulations, and scalable web application backends that do not demand large in-memory databases or localized NVMe caching.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.94-376 is a compute-oriented virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. Given its dense multi-threaded core count and compute-optimized memory allocation, the instance provides cost efficiency for highly parallelized, compute-intensive tasks. Primary workloads include large-scale batch processing, distributed software compilation, parallel simulation workloads, video transcoding, and scalable application tier hosting.
